questions.question: What inverted device architecture and active-layer processing strategy did this study use for flexible PM6:Y6 cells?

options.A: ITO/ZnO/PM6:Y6/MoO3/Ag, with the ZnO and active layer slot-die coated on PET
options.B: ITO/PEDOT:PSS/PM6:Y6/LiF/Al, with the active layer spin-coated on glass
options.C: PET/Ag/MoO3/PM6:Y6/ZnO/ITO, with the active layer blade-coated under nitrogen
options.D: ITO/ZnO/Y6:PCBM/PM6/MoO3/Ag, with the active layer printed from chlorobenzene

questions.rationale: The flexible device used the inverted ITO/ZnO/PM6:Y6/MoO3/Ag stack; ZnO and active layer were deposited using the roll-coater/slot-die process.
questions.evidence_quote: the device is made with the following inverted geometry: ITO/ZnO/PM6:Y6/MoO3/Ag.

questions.question: Why was the slot-die coating assembly heated during deposition of PM6:Y6?

options.A: PM6 exhibits temperature-dependent aggregation and must remain liquid during coating
options.B: Y6 crystallizes irreversibly unless the substrate is cooled below 60 °C
options.C: The PET substrate requires heating to prevent silver diffusion
options.D: The green solvent o-xylene cannot dissolve either component at room temperature

questions.rationale: The paper notes PM6 temperature-dependent aggregation and describes heating the substrate, syringe, tube, and slot-die head so the solution stays hot throughout coating.
questions.evidence_quote: the PM6 exhibits temperature-dependent aggregation (TDA) behavior and therefore needs to be heated to remain liquid throughout the slot-die coating procedure

questions.question: Which conditions were used for the ZnO electron-transport-layer coating before its anneal?

options.A: 75 °C substrate temperature, 0.06 mL min−1 ink flow, and 1.08 m min−1 drum speed
options.B: 100 °C substrate temperature, 0.12 mL min−1 ink flow, and 1.5 m min−1 drum speed
options.C: 60 °C substrate temperature, 0.06 mL min−1 ink flow, and 1.5 m min−1 drum speed
options.D: 75 °C substrate temperature, 0.12 mL min−1 ink flow, and 1.08 m min−1 drum speed

questions.rationale: ZnO was coated at 75 °C with 0.06 mL/min flow and 1.08 m/min drum speed, then annealed at 100 °C for 10 minutes in air.
questions.evidence_quote: The ZnO nanoparticle ink (ETL) was coated at a substrate temperature of 75 °C with a 0.06 mL/min flow rate and a drum speed of 1.08 m/min.

questions.question: Why did the authors select 100 °C rather than 120 °C as the optimal active-layer coating temperature?

options.A: At 120 °C the average fill factor fell to 42.2% versus 47.10% at 100 °C, offsetting the higher current; edge aggregation also created stripe inhomogeneities
options.B: At 120 °C the short-circuit current fell below that of 60 °C, despite an increased fill factor
options.C: At 100 °C the blend absorption red-shifted, while 120 °C eliminated Y6 absorption
options.D: At 120 °C the active layer became thinner than 100 nm and could not absorb visible light

questions.rationale: Although higher coating temperature improves current, the 120 °C devices had lower average FF, and drying above 100 °C caused material aggregation at the stripe edges.
questions.evidence_quote: However, the average FF value of 42.2% is lower for the 120 °C coating than for the 100 °C coating (47.10%).

questions.question: Which light-intensity result supported reduced bimolecular recombination as one reason for the optimized performance at 100 °C?

options.A: The exponent S in JSC∝Pin^S was 0.978, the closest to unity among the temperature-tested devices
options.B: The exponent S was 0.987, the closest to unity among the thickness-tested devices
options.C: The VOC-versus-ln(Pin) slope was below kT/q only at 100 °C
options.D: The photocurrent saturation voltage exceeded 2 V only for devices coated at 120 °C

questions.rationale: For temperature optimization, the S value closest to unity was 0.978 at 100 °C, which the authors linked to reduced bimolecular recombination.
questions.evidence_quote: the S value closest to unity (S = 0.978) is obtained by coating at 100 °C, implying that one of the reasons for the optimized performance is due to reduced bimolecular recombination.

questions.question: How did active-layer thickness affect average PCE, and which thickness/concentration combination gave the thickness-optimization champion?

options.A: Average PCE rose with thickness; 217 nm from 24 mg/mL ink gave the 6.3% champion
options.B: Average PCE fell with thickness; 101 nm from 12 mg/mL ink gave the 6.3% champion
options.C: Average PCE peaked at 154 nm; 16 mg/mL ink gave a 7.2% champion
options.D: Average PCE was constant from 101 to 217 nm; 116 nm from 28 mg/mL ink gave the 7.2% champion

questions.rationale: Average PCE increased as the active layer thickened, and the highest thickness-study device reached 6.3% at 217 nm using 24 mg/mL ink.
questions.evidence_quote: The highest PCE obtained in the thickness optimization is 6.3%, with an FF of 49.0%, when coating with ink concentration of 24 mg/ml, equivalent to 217 nm thickness.

questions.question: What recombination conclusion did the authors draw from VOC versus ln(Pin) slopes for the temperature-optimized devices?

options.A: Trap-assisted recombination was dominant because all measured slopes were higher than kT/q
options.B: Second-order recombination dominated because all slopes were lower than kT/q
options.C: Bimolecular recombination was absent because the slopes all equaled kT/q
options.D: No conclusion was possible because the VOC slope did not depend on light intensity

questions.rationale: The paper uses slopes greater than kT/q to infer trap-assisted recombination as the dominant mechanism in these devices.
questions.evidence_quote: The results suggest that the trap-assisted recombination in our devices is the dominant one (Figure S6b ), as all the obtained slope values are higher than kT/q.

questions.question: For the [1:1:0.2] PM6:Y6:PC61BM blend, what changes did the study report relative to binary PM6:Y6 devices processed at the same temperature?

options.A: Average JSC increased by 12%, and the average ternary PCE was 6.6%
options.B: Average JSC decreased by 12%, and the average ternary PCE was 6.7%
options.C: Average fill factor increased by 12 percentage points, and PCE reached 7.2% on average
options.D: The average PCE stayed at 5.8%, but the current was unchanged because PCBM added no photocurrent

questions.rationale: The 1:1:0.2 ternary blend yielded a 12% higher average JSC than binary devices at 100 °C and a 6.6% average PCE; the champion ternary device reached 7.2%.
questions.evidence_quote: On average, a 12% higher JSC is obtained from the [1:1:0.2] ternary blend compared with binary devices coated at the same temperature (100 °C) with a 24 mg/mL concentration in O-XY (Table S2 ).

questions.question: Which charge-generation and charge-collection probabilities were reported for binary versus ternary blends, and which ternary ratio performed best on each metric?

options.A: Dissociation: 93.7% binary, 96.3% at 1:1:0.2 and 95.7% at 1:1.1:0.1; collection: 69.6%, 77.7%, and 73.2%, respectively
options.B: Dissociation: 69.6% binary, 77.7% at 1:1:0.2 and 73.2% at 1:1.1:0.1; collection: 93.7%, 96.3%, and 95.7%, respectively
options.C: Dissociation: 93.7% binary, 95.7% at 1:1:0.2 and 96.3% at 1:1.1:0.1; collection: 69.6%, 73.2%, and 77.7%, respectively
options.D: Dissociation: 96.3% binary, 93.7% at 1:1:0.2 and 95.7% at 1:1.1:0.1; collection: 77.7%, 69.6%, and 73.2%, respectively

questions.rationale: Adding PCBM raised dissociation and collection probabilities; the 1:1:0.2 ternary ratio had the higher reported values for both metrics.
questions.evidence_quote: The dissociation probability is 93.7% for the binary device, significantly lower than 96.3% and 95.7% obtained for the ternary 1:1:0.2 and 1:1.1:0.1 devices respectively.

questions.question: What dark-storage stability did encapsulated binary and ternary devices retain under the reported ISOS-D-1 test?

options.A: Ternary cells retained 99.4% after 1050 h, while binary cells retained over 97% after more than 1500 h
options.B: Ternary cells retained over 97% after 1500 h, while binary cells retained 99.4% after 1050 h
options.C: Both device types retained 90% after 1000 h, with no difference by blend composition
options.D: Ternary cells degraded by 99.4% after 1050 h, while binary cells degraded by 97% after 1500 h

questions.rationale: The study reports exceptional dark-storage retention for both formulations, with separate test durations for ternary and binary devices.
questions.evidence_quote: The average PCEs measured after 1050 hours for the ternary device retained 99.4% of the average initial value, whereas the average PCEs of binary devices retained more than 97% of the initial average PCE after more than 1500 hours of storage.
